Iditarod Trail.fact: The federal Bureau of Land Management coordinates cooperative management of the trail and is the primary point of contact for matters involving the entire trail.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: The statewide non-profit _____
Iditarod Trail.fact: The statewide non-profit Iditarod National Historic Trail Inc.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: It is a common myth that the race commemorates the dogsled relay known as the _____ "Serum Run" from Nenana to Nome
Iditarod Trail.fact: It is a common myth that the race commemorates the dogsled relay called the 1925 "Serum Run" from Nenana to Nome.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: in the early _____ to encourage the designation of the Iditarod Trail as a National Historic Trail, bring the dying tradition of dog sledding back to the villages of Alaska, and promote the sport of c
Iditarod Trail.fact: in the early 1973 to encourage the designation of the Iditarod Trail as a National Historic Trail, bring the dying tradition of dog sledding back to the villages of Alaska, and promote the sport of competitive dogsled racing.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: Today the race follows much of the primary route of the _____, with a segment alternating north or south, depending on the year
Iditarod Trail.fact: Today the race follows much of the primary route of the Iditarod National Historic Trail, with a segment alternating north or south, depending on the year. (These segments are also part of the Iditarod National Historic Trail).

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: (These segments are also part of the _____)
Iditarod Trail.fact: Today the race follows much of the primary route of the Iditarod National Historic Trail, with a segment alternating north or south, depending on the year. (These segments are also part of the Iditarod National Historic Trail).

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: Every odd year (i.e., _____), the race travels the south route from Ophir to Kaltag through the ghost town of Iditarod
Iditarod Trail.fact: Every odd year (i.e., 2011), the race travels the south route from Ophir to Kaltag through the ghost town of Iditarod.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: On even years, the race travels north from Ophir through Ruby and _____ to Kaltag
Iditarod Trail.fact: On even years, the race travels north from Ophir through Ruby and Galena to Kaltag.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: The _____ Serum Run followed 500 miles (800 km) of trail (now designated as the Iditarod National Historic Trail system) between Ruby and Nome
Iditarod Trail.fact: The 1925 Serum Run followed 500 miles (800 km) of trail (now designated as the Iditarod National Historic Trail system) between Ruby and Nome.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: The Iditarod Trail Invitational human powered race for bikers, runners and skiers also follows the Iditarod Trail from Knik to McGrath with a 350-mile race and to Nome in a _____-mile race
Iditarod Trail.fact: The Iditarod Trail Invitational human powered race for bikers, runners and skiers also follows the Iditarod Trail from Knik to McGrath with a 350-mile race and to Nome in a 1000-mile race.

Iditarod Trail.subject: Indian Heritage
Iditarod Trail.question: In _____, Sunny Stroeer of Utah became the first woman to ski the 1,000-mile Iditarod Trail Invitational
Iditarod Trail.fact: In 2024, Sunny Stroeer of Utah became the first woman to ski the 1,000-mile Iditarod Trail Invitational.
